newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's rating outlook improves - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's rating outlook improves - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday that the credit rating outlook for Australia was improving, citing the government's steady fiscal policy framework and the central bank's prudent monetary policy stance.

The ratings agency said in a commentary issued from its New York head office that any change in Australia's Aa2 long-term rating would depend on the nation further reducing its reliance on foreign savings.

"For the most part, the more favorable outlook stems from a steady strengthening of the fiscal policy framework, combined with the retention of a prudent monetary policy stance since the early 1990s," Moody's said in a statement.

It also said economic growth and fiscal-tightening measures in the past few years have had a positive influence on the underlying budgetary position of the government sector, noting that the underlying deficit is projected to be less than one percent of gross domestic product this financial year.
Moody's said Australian national and state governments were also improving financial flexibility by using proceeds from privatisation initiatives to reduce debt burdens.

"More significantly, from a credit quality perspective, is the fact that the narrowing of the underlying fiscal gap has had a positive influence on the level of national savings. This, in turn, has somewhat reduced the country's reliance on foreign savings in the financing of investment activitiy," the agency added.

"Nonetheless, as implied by the recurring current account deficit of the balance of payment, the country still faces a sizeable gap between its own sources of savings and current levels of investment," Moody's said.

"Of importance to the rating in the future, Moody's explained, will be the country's capacity to further reduce its reliance on foreign savings, either by continued improvement in the fiscal performance of its public sector, or by a rise in the level of private sector savings."
